findings.claim: The new core-prefix line tells the verifier to resolve a memorycard topic 'via mem_search, then mem_get', but the verifier's tool list gives it only mcp__memorycard__mem_get, with no mem_search. Before this change the line ('Engram topic via mem_get_observation') matched the verifier's one tool. In memorycard, mem_get replaces mem_get_observation, so it reads by id. A verifier prompt that locates an artifact by memorycard topic_key cannot do the step it is told to do. Because the line also says a missing locator is a blocker, the verifier would stop as blocked. hasMemoryTool() keeps the line whenever any mcp__memorycard__ tool is listed, so the generator emits this mismatch. The same mismatch is in pi/agents/verifier.md and codex/agents/verifier.toml.
proof_refs: diff hunk agents/verifier.md: tools '...Bash, mcp__memorycard__mem_get' with line '+...memorycard topic via mem_search, then mem_get...'
engine/agentgen/roles.go hasMemoryTool: strings.HasPrefix(tool, "mcp__memorycard__") keeps the full line for verifier

findings.claim: On Pi, every role's memory tools now use the names mcp__memorycard__mem_*, and the code comment admits these names are an unverified assumption. If gentle-pi or pi-mcp-adapter does not register those exact names, gentle-pi drops them without a warning (lib/agents-runner.ts:241, per the comment). Pi roles would then lose every memory tool while their prompt still sends them to memorycard topics. The test TestThePiToolsOfEveryRoleAreNamesTheInstalledSourcesRegister now puts these assumed names in its 'known' set, so it cannot catch a wrong name, even though the test's name says it checks registered names. The base mapping (bare mem_* names from gentle-engram, which is said to be uninstalled) was likely broken too, so this change cannot be shown to make Pi worse.
proof_refs: engine/agentgen/roles.go piToolNames comment: 'This one is an assumption, not verified'
